tldr: Headlines across all 13 country buckets overwhelmingly frame the Shelton-Alcaraz quarterfinal as a historic sporting spectacle anchored by its record-late 3:33am finish and the dramatic five-set upset, while the UK tabloid and one Italian outlet are alone in foregrounding Alcaraz's physical distress at title level.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline foregrounding Alcaraz's vomiting as a tabloid spectacle ('vomit-stained 3.33am nightmare') rather than the match result — the health-distress angle is invisible in every other title worldwide.

Only headline leading with Alcaraz's gracious reaction ('I leave with a smile') rather than the match result or record-late finish — the player's emotional response, not the outcome or spectacle, is the advertised story.

bottom_line: The headline layer sells a single story globally: a record-late sporting spectacle defined by the 3:33am finish and a five-set upset — but only the UK tabloid broadcasts Alcaraz's physical condition, and only the Philippines outlet surfaces his emotional reaction, while the match's broader all-American-semifinal significance is absent from virtually all front pages.
